purpose: Law-1 visible parked channel. Nothing here was dropped. Each entry is uncertainty about whether the pattern APPLIES, not about severity. Cull at triage (/ledger), never by withholding from the run a human reviews.

parked.title: Sub-wei truncation forfeiture on every flush: lastUpdate advances unconditionally, including when settled == 0
parked.reason: Magnitude is dust and each triggering call costs a real paid mint, so the applicability of the truncation-forfeiture pattern is genuinely uncertain rather than the severity. Parked, not dropped: the mechanism is real (s.lastUpdate = block.timestamp is unconditional, so fractional accrual below 1 wei is discarded), and D-26-01's unconditional flush means any batchMint cadence triggers it (<=1 wei per stream per call, <=~50k wei over a 7-day window at 12s blocks).

doNotCollapse.why: UPSTREAM DECISION 4, not re-litigated: aaebb4b9b0 is the window-RESET mechanism; this is TRUNCATION. Different mechanisms, different fixes. Collapsing them would lose one.

parked.reopenAt: Escalate if a decimals-sensitive nudge token makes the per-call truncation a whole unit rather than sub-wei (cf. ledger 51aed27661, the decimals-blind DUST_THRESHOLD class on the batchMinter side, where a 6-dp token turned a claimed 10^-12 into up to 0.999999 whole units per batch).

parked.title: registerStream lacks nonReentrant while _settle makes an outbound transfer, unlike both its siblings
parked.reason: Mechanism CLEARED by tier-2 (code-findings.md section 1.1 row 10 and section 5): _settle completes first, a reentrant collectNudge credits a measured receipt and recomputes over the old duration, then registerStream overwrites duration/rewardPerSecond/lastUpdate from the CURRENT s.buffer at :139 -- consistent, no over-statement, and hook-token-only regardless. Parked rather than killed because the GUARD ASYMMETRY itself is unexplained: the contract's two other mutating entry points are both nonReentrant and this one is not, so the safety is incidental to write ordering rather than enforced. A future edit that moved a write above _settle would make it live with no compiler or reviewer signal.
parked.preconditions: onlyOwner caller plus a transfer-hook (weird-ERC20) nudge token; the token half is C4-permanently-invalid standalone.
parked.reopenAt: Reopen if any state write in registerStream moves ahead of the _settle call at :134, or if a non-owner path to registerStream is ever added.

parked.title: batchMint recipient is unvalidated beyond non-zero; recipient == address(this) would route _payRewards to self
parked.reason: GENUINELY UNRESOLVED -- the only entry here that no tier adjudicated. Tier-1 guessed it unreachable via the ERC1155 receiver requirement on the mint at :650, but tier-2 (section 5, ERC1155 row) CORRECTED the profile on the adjacent point: it confirmed the receive hook does fire on a caller-chosen recipient, contradicting the profile's claim that no inbound hook surface exists. That correction removes the basis for the unreachability guess without resolving it. Needs a read of whether BatchNFTMinterMultiToken implements onERC1155Received (and hence whether it can be its own recipient), which requires the yield-claim-nft NFTMinterV2 mint path.
parked.nextStep: Read yield-claim-nft@d4cc563 NFTMinterV2._executeMint:196 (OZ _mint acceptance check) against BatchNFTMinterMultiToken's declared interfaces. If the batchMinter is NOT an ERC1155 receiver the path is closed by revert; if it is, trace whether _payRewards(address(this), snapshot) plus the step-10 refund can compose into a self-credit.

relatedLedger.why: Already records the mid-loop onERC1155Received surface as real-but-held, and notes the project's MockERC1155.mint() skips _checkOnERC1155Received entirely -- so the project's own test suite cannot answer this question either.

parked.title: rewardPerSecond * elapsed overflow at absurd buffer with duration == 1 bricks the pair and hence every batchMint
parked.reason: Requires a ~1e50 buffer, which is not reachable with any real asset, so the pattern's applicability is near-nil. Parked for the COUPLING only, which is the part worth a human eye: an overflow here would revert both collectNudge AND pullPendingStream for the pair permanently, and via D-26-01's unisolated flush loop that bricks every batchMint with no owner escape other than de-whitelisting the token (which then strands the buffer -- ledger 4a1d8edc92).
parked.reopenAt: Reopen if a nudge token with an extreme supply/decimals combination is ever whitelisted, or if PRECISION or duration bounds change (duration == 1 is currently permitted -- only duration == 0 is rejected at :126).

notParkedButRecorded.reason: Not parked because it is DISPROVEN, not uncertain. yield-claim-nft@d4cc563 NFTMinterV2._executeMint has exactly one return statement, a literal true on the sole success path; there is no 'return false' anywhere in the contract and every failure mode is a hard revert. The discarded bool at BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:650 (and legacy BatchNFTMinter.sol:287) can therefore never mask a no-op mint that debits budget. See dedup-report.md section 3.1.

Not parked because the substantive limb is already tracked in visible ledger entries (aaebb4b9b0 open, 6f46ec80f1 open, b58b172e2a fixed). The two NudgeStreamer instances are Slither mis-attribution (settled > 0 and accrued > buffer are not timestamp thresholds); the other 65 are pre-existing window arithmetic in the unchanged staker family. See dedup-report.md section 3.2.

Leg B (aggregate buffer over-statement) was killed upstream and machine-confirmed by tier-3 (452k+ fuzzed calls, two engines, mutation-verified harness). NOT parked. But tier3/symbolic.md did not exist at dedup time, and tier-3 nominated exactly this property (INV-1) for a Halmos proof. If the symbolic run returns a counterexample under a plain ERC20, Leg B revives and D-26-01 reopens at Medium under its own written reopen trigger. A Halmos TIMEOUT is not a proof either way. See dedup-report.md section 7 item 1.
